clue.text: One relatively far back puts pressure on an engineer

indicators.note: in an across clue, putting one piece on another places it after

parts.note: taken as written
CE stands for civil engineer
stress is pressure or strain

explanation.surface: Someone bullies an engineer by leaning on them hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One relatively far back' is a playful way of saying a female relative from generations ago.
explanation.definitionFit: A female forebear is a relation from far back in the family line.

clue.text: Jezebel's husband has a costume without it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: without tells us to drop the word it from the costume word

parts.note: a habit is a costume, as worn by a monk or rider
taken as written

explanation.surface: A biblical queen's spouse turns up in an outfit missing a piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes IT from HABIT, leaving HAB.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Old Testament, the king of Israel married to Jezebel was this ruler.

clue.text: Dramatist gets mark after examination orally

indicators.note: orally means the phrase is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: to check off is to tick something once it has been examined

explanation.surface: A playwright receives a grade following an oral test.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a viva, but 'orally' signals a sound-alike: 'check off' said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian author of The Cherry Orchard and The Seagull was a celebrated playwright.

clue.text: Descriptions of attractive model that's well placed

definitions.meaning: an artist's model holding a pose who looks good is literally posing attractively while seated
comfortably situated, in a strong position

explanation.surface: Words that describe a good-looking model who is in a fortunate position.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means being in a comfortable, advantageous position; literally it describes a seated, good-looking model.

clue.text: Seize, taking leader down a peg, and fine to maximum

indicators.note: the first letter is shifted one place further down the word

parts.note: to arrest is to seize or apprehend

explanation.surface: Someone grabs a boss, humbles them and fines them as heavily as possible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking leader down a peg' moves the opening A of ARREST one place along, making RAREST. 'fine' is an adjective, not a penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: Rare can mean exceptionally good, so the superlative is the finest of all.

clue.text: Break in journey to sort post deliveries

indicators.note: sorting the word post rearranges its letters

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries by a bowler

explanation.surface: A postal worker pauses mid-route to sort the mail before delivering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to sort' rearranges POST into STOP. Deliveries are cricket balls bowled, and six make an OVER.
explanation.definitionFit: A short stay on the way somewhere is a pause partway through a trip.

clue.text: Warm island? Think it over

definitions.meaning: to heat wine or ale with spices
an island of the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether to holiday on a warm island and decides to reflect.
explanation.definitionFit: The one word means to heat and spice a drink, names a Hebridean island, and means to ponder.

clue.text: Tool needed in lute's construction

indicators.note: construction means the letters are built into a new arrangement

parts.note: the letters of lute plus the s

explanation.surface: A tool is required to build a lute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'construction' rearranges IN and LUTES.
explanation.definitionFit: An implement, especially one used in the kitchen, is a tool.

clue.text: Not properly prepared to survive a short time

parts.note: to last is to endure or survive
a minute is a brief moment

explanation.surface: Someone unprepared hopes to get through a brief spell.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done at the final moment is rushed and so lacks proper preparation.

clue.text: Help one in casino

definitions.meaning: a person who helps or encourages, especially in wrongdoing
a person who gambles, read as a punter

explanation.surface: An accomplice helps someone at the gaming tables.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense hears the word as 'a better', someone placing bets.
explanation.definitionFit: An accomplice who assists is one sense; split up it becomes a gambler who wagers money.

clue.text: Very big applause heard for flyers

parts.note: OS is the abbreviation for outsize

indicators.note: heard means a word that sounds like the next piece

parts.note: praise is acclaim or applause

explanation.surface: Huge clapping rings out for a team of aviators.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flyers' are birds here, not pilots or rugby players.
explanation.definitionFit: These fish-eating raptors are birds, and birds are flyers.

clue.text: Obsession with state of France in 1939?

definitions.meaning: a fixation that fills the mind
France was not yet under German control until 1940, so it was in a pre-invasion state

explanation.surface: A fixation with how France stood on the eve of war.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as PRE-OCCUPATION, the second sense is the period before the Germans occupied France.
explanation.definitionFit: A mental fixation fills the mind; split with a hyphen it means the time before a military takeover.

clue.text: Cashier not working in shop

indicators.note: working means the letters are put to work in a new order

explanation.surface: A cashier is off duty in a store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' looks like it negates 'working', but it is fodder: CASHIER and NOT are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A retail branch belonging to a group of stores is a kind of shop.

clue.text: As time goes by, he plays a lot of Brazilian music

definitions.text: As time goes by, he plays

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, its tail dropped

parts.note: samba is a Brazilian dance music

explanation.surface: A pianist plays a lot of Brazilian rhythms as the years pass.
explanation.walkthrough: In the film Casablanca the pianist is asked to 'Play it, Sam', and the song he plays is 'As Time Goes By'. 'a lot of' drops the last two letters of SAMBA.
explanation.definitionFit: The pianist character in Casablanca performs the song As Time Goes By.

clue.text: Hamper brought by Santa's reindeer for traditional performer

parts.note: to clog is to obstruct or hamper
Dancer is one of Santa's reindeer

explanation.surface: A Christmas basket arrives with a reindeer for a folk entertainer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamper' looks like a gift basket but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer of the clog dance, a folk tradition in wooden shoes, is a traditional entertainer.

clue.text: Adore to eat a good herb

indicators.note: to eat means one word takes the others inside it

parts.note: to adore is to love
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone loves to eat a nice herb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to eat' puts A and G inside LOVE.
explanation.definitionFit: This umbelliferous plant with celery-like leaves is used as a culinary herb.

clue.text: Me gettin' high on this?

parts.note: taken as written
scaling is climbing high, written with the dropped g to match

explanation.surface: Someone drawls a question about whether this drug is what sent them up.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: the drug makes you high, and the wordplay ME plus 'scalin'' says climbing high.
explanation.definitionFit: A hallucinogen from peyote cactus is a drug that gets users high.

clue.text: For preference, taking companion aboard ship

indicators.note: aboard means one piece is taken on inside another

parts.note: sooner means rather, by preference
CH is Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: Given the choice, someone brings a friend on board a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For preference' reads like a lead-in phrase but supplies the wordplay; 'ship' is the definition at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A fore-and-aft rigged sailing vessel with two or more masts is a kind of ship.

clue.text: Cheap break by plane rejected

indicators.note: rejected means the plane's name is thrown back, read the other way

parts.note: a MiG is a Russian fighter plane
a crack is a break

explanation.surface: A budget getaway by air is turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns MIG into GIM. 'break' is a fracture, not a holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Something showy but of shoddy make is cheap and tawdry.

clue.text: In truth, a year is such a tenure for dignitary

definitions.text: In truth, a year is such a tenure for dignitary

parts.words: In truth, a year is such a tenure for dignitary
parts.note: a civic leader of a town traditionally holds office for one year, so the clue describes that term of office

explanation.surface: A remark that a certain civic official typically serves only twelve months.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'dignitary' is a town's civic head, who usually holds the post for a single year.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes the office of a town's civic chief, whose term is typically a year.

clue.text: Team dismissed by unpleasant attack

parts.note: a batsman dismissed in cricket is out
a fit is a sudden bout, as of coughing

explanation.surface: A side is knocked out by a nasty assault.
explanation.definitionFit: A group working together, such as a band or company, is an outfit or team.

clue.text: Medley, for a change, including jazz piece

indicators.note: including means one piece goes inside the other
change means the letters of for a are shuffled

parts.note: a rag is a piece of ragtime music

explanation.surface: For variety, a mixed programme features some jazz.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a change' rearranges FOR A into FARO, and 'including' puts RAG inside it: FAR-RAG-O.
explanation.definitionFit: A confused mixture or hotchpotch is a medley.

clue.text: Flinched, seeing footballer finally breaking leg

indicators.note: breaking means a letter breaks into the word for leg

parts.note: the shank is the lower leg

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of footballer

explanation.surface: Someone recoils on seeing a player snap his leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives R, and 'breaking' puts it inside SHANK.
explanation.definitionFit: To shrink is to recoil or flinch, and this is its past tense.

clue.text: Johnson has a surprised expression

parts.note: taken as written
My! is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: Johnson looks astonished.
explanation.walkthrough: Johnson is the pioneering aviator Amy Johnson, not a politician.
explanation.definitionFit: The English pilot who flew solo to Australia in 1930 had the surname Johnson.

clue.text: Child supposes she pays her back after a falling out

definitions.text: Child supposes she pays her back after a falling out

parts.words: Child supposes she pays her back after a falling out
parts.note: a child believes a magical visitor leaves money once a tooth has fallen out, not after a quarrel

explanation.surface: A youngster imagines a friend will repay her after an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a falling out' looks like a quarrel but is a milk tooth coming loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Children believe this folklore figure leaves a coin under the pillow for a lost milk tooth.

clue.text: Succeed in securing a cart

indicators.note: securing means one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: to win is to succeed
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone triumphs in obtaining a wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a farm wagon is a cart.

clue.text: Series of films that keep going

definitions.meaning: the long-running British comedy film series

explanation.surface: A film franchise that just keeps running.
explanation.walkthrough: The Carry On films are a long run of bawdy British comedies.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a British comedy film series and also means to continue.

clue.text: A short story with two clever people and a woodcutter

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a lie is a story or fib

indicators.note: two means the piece is used twice

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a graduate

explanation.surface: A brief tale features a pair of brainy characters and a forester.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims LIE to LI, and 'two' doubles BA.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Arabian Nights tale, the hero who found the thieves' cave was a poor woodcutter.

clue.text: Tiny crustaceans, a thousand lost in stream

indicators.note: lost means the thousand is taken away

parts.note: krill are tiny crustaceans eaten by whales
K is the abbreviation for a thousand

explanation.surface: Tiny shrimps, a thousand of them, vanish in a brook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' removes K from KRILL.
explanation.definitionFit: A small brook or rivulet is a little stream.

clue.text: Analysed colour fencing came in

indicators.note: came in means one piece enters the other

parts.note: brown is a colour
kendo is Japanese fencing with bamboo swords

explanation.surface: A tan-coloured swordsman entered the room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fencing' looks like a barrier around the colour, but it is the Japanese sport; 'Analysed' means split into parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A total broken down into parts has been itemised and so analysed.
